root_motivation: An agent that found another agent's shared tool in `host.catalog.search` cannot name its author. `host.whoami` (`src/control.rs`) returns the caller's own `namespace`, `display_name`, `plan`, `source_class` and `client_name`, and only to the caller. `tools.visibility` and `groups` (`migrations/0013_sharing.sql`) let a tenant expose tools to others, but no table maps a tenant to anything another tenant may read about it. `display_name` is `NOT NULL` with no uniqueness (`0001_init.sql:7`), so it cannot serve as an address: two tenants can both be "ops-bot".
user_persona: An agent that has discovered another agent's shared tool (via `host.catalog.search`) or that wants to be discoverable itself -- it needs to resolve a namespace or handle to a readable card (name, description, tags, contact policy) without ever learning a billing field, key hash, or call log; secondarily the operator (Joe), who needs `admin.agent.lookup`/`admin.agent.handle_release` to recover a squatted or abusive handle.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a fresh tenant with no profile row, When it calls `host.agent.whoami`, Then the result has `address` equal to its namespace, `handle: null`, `contact_policy: "open"`, and no `key_hash`, `billing_ref` or `stripe_customer_id` key.

Given tenant A claims `@indexer` via `host.agent.profile_set`, When tenant B calls `host.agent.lookup("@indexer")`, Then B receives A's card with `address` equal to A's namespace and the card omits every billing and key field.
Given `@indexer` is held by A, When B calls `host.agent.profile_set(handle="Indexer")`, Then B gets structured error `handle_taken` whose body names no tenant, and A's handle is unchanged.

Given a namespace that does not exist, a tenant disabled via `admin.tenant_disable`, and a tenant deleted via `admin.tenant_delete`, When another tenant looks each up, Then all three responses are `agent_not_found` with byte-identical bodies.

Given A has tags `["rag","indexing"]` and description "nightly index builder", When B calls `host.agent.search(tag="rag")` and `host.agent.search(query="INDEX")`, Then both results include A exactly once and exclude a disabled tenant with the same tag.

Given 60 profiled tenants, When B calls `host.agent.search(limit=25)` twice following the returned cursor, Then the two pages are disjoint, ordered by handle then namespace, and together contain 50 cards with a third page holding the remaining 10.
Given A holds `@indexer` and is deleted through `admin.tenant_delete`, When B claims `@indexer`, Then the claim succeeds and `agent_profiles` has no row for A's former id.
Given 1 000 profiled tenants in a warm database, When 200 sequential `host.agent.lookup` calls run, Then p95 latency is under 50 ms.

Given a handle in the reserved list, When any tenant claims it, Then the response is `handle_reserved`; and given the admin key calls `admin.agent.handle_release("@indexer")`, Then the handle is free and one `admin_events` row records the release.
Given a tenant created with the `x-mcphost-synthetic` header, When another tenant looks it up, Then its card carries `synthetic: true`.

scope: New table `agent_profiles(tenant_id PK, handle TEXT UNIQUE NULL, description, tags_json, contact_policy DEFAULT 'open', updated_at)` in migration 0020; every tenant reads as a profile card even with no row (defaults applied at read) (P0, AC1).
`host.agent.whoami` returns `{address, handle, display_name, contact_policy, plan}` -- never `key_hash`, `billing_ref` or `stripe_customer_id` (P0, AC1).

`host.agent.profile_set(handle?, description?, tags?, contact_policy?)`: handle matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,31}$`, stored lower-case, atomic claim-or-fail via a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction; a taken handle returns structured error `handle_taken` naming nothing about the holder; a reserved handle (`admin`, `host`, `mcphost`, `system`) returns `handle_reserved` (P0/P1, AC3/AC9).

`host.agent.lookup(address)` accepts `@handle` or `t_...` and returns the public card; unknown, disabled, and deleted tenants all return `agent_not_found` with byte-identical bodies so search-by-error cannot leak existence (P0, AC2/AC4).

`host.agent.search(query?, tag?, limit<=50, cursor?)` matches tag exactly or query as a case-insensitive substring of handle/display name/description, excludes disabled tenants, orders by `handle NULLS LAST, namespace`, and pages via an offset cursor (P0, AC5/AC6).

`last_seen` derived from the tenant's most recent authenticated request (`tenants.last_seen_unix`), rounded to the minute; profile cascades on tenant delete so a released handle is claimable again immediately (P0, AC7).

`admin.agent.lookup(address)` and `admin.agent.handle_release(address)` on the admin key, gated by the existing `Auth::Admin` resolution and `dispatch_admin_tool` path; release writes an `admin_events` row (P1, AC9).
`synthetic` tenants' cards carry `synthetic: true` so harness agents are distinguishable from real ones in search results (P1, AC10).

New `src/agents.rs` module for card assembly, handle validation, and the new `Db` methods (`agent_profile`, `set_agent_profile`, `lookup_agent`, `list_agent_cards`, `release_handle`); errors use the existing `AppError::Structured{code, message, data}` shape.
non_goals: Sending messages -- PRD-mcphost-agent-inbox owns the inbox; this PRD only makes the recipient nameable.
Presence heartbeats beyond `last_seen` derived from the tenant's last authenticated call.
Sub-identities under one tenant, or handle scoping under operator domains -- open question in the vision, deferred past this build.

`host.agent.search` `source_class` filter (P2) and the corpus-task/harness-probe wiring for AC9's admin-release path in this build -- deferred, see PRD frontmatter `deferred_acs` / `mock_justifications` where applicable.

additional.no_sensitive_fields_leaked: every card-producing path (whoami, lookup, admin.agent.lookup, search) asserts the absence of `key_hash`, `billing_ref`, and `stripe_customer_id` in its own test -- verified by grep across agentdir_ac01_ac02_ac03_ac04's whoami/lookup assertions (PRD AC1/AC2).
additional.agent_not_found_byte_identical: `host.agent.lookup` on an unknown namespace, a disabled tenant, and a deleted tenant must return byte-identical `agent_not_found` bodies -- verified by agentdir_ac01_ac02_ac03_ac04's AC4 test comparing all three responses directly (PRD AC4, Technical considerations).
additional.handle_claim_atomicity: `Db::set_agent_profile`'s handle-uniqueness check-then-insert runs inside a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction so two concurrent claims for the same handle cannot both succeed (PRD AC3, Requirement 3).
additional.no_admin_auth_bypass: the two new admin.* tools (admin.agent.lookup, admin.agent.handle_release) are wired through the existing dispatch_admin_tool path, gated by the existing Auth::Admin resolution -- no new admin authentication or authorization path is introduced (PRD Requirement 8).

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't an agent that calls another tenant's shared tool learn who built it?
five_whys_trace.a: `host.whoami` (src/control.rs) returns the caller's own namespace/display_name/plan/source_class/client_name, and only to the caller -- no tool maps a tenant to anything another tenant may read about it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't `display_name` just serve as that address today?
five_whys_trace.a: `display_name` is NOT NULL with no uniqueness constraint (0001_init.sql:7) -- two tenants can both be "ops-bot", so it cannot resolve to exactly one tenant.

five_whys_trace.q: Why wasn't this solved when the mesh registry gap was first found?
five_whys_trace.a: The parked mdcollab-agent-registry PRD (2026-07-20) recorded the same gap but never shipped; it did settle the one load-bearing decision this PRD keeps -- identity anchored to the authenticated principal, never self-asserted.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not let a tenant self-assert its own address, the way agorabus's session_id works?
five_whys_trace.a: Prior fleet art shows the failure mode directly: agorabus peers are identified by a client-chosen session_id, safe only on a 0600 local socket and unsafe on a public host -- mcphost tenants are reachable over the public host, so self-assertion is not an option here.

five_whys_trace.q: Why build a handle and search on top of the always-available namespace address rather than just the namespace?
five_whys_trace.a: A namespace (`t_xxxxxxxx`) is not a name an agent would say aloud or remember; a handle is optional so opting out of a name never opts a tenant out of the mesh (namespace lookup still works), and search is what makes an unnamed but tagged/described tenant discoverable at all.

ambiguities_resolved.question: The findings file records the reference Python client seeing well-formed ttlMs/cacheScope on an unauthenticated tools/list, which the code says is impossible. Which is right?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Almost certainly a client-side deserialization default printed where the wire had nothing (rmcp's own mirror of that shape defaults to ttl_ms 0 / cache_scope Private). Settled by a test rather than an argument: AC2 asserts on the serialized wire JSON, not a deserialized model.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Requirement 9 offers two ways to fix the middleware doc/scope mismatch: re-scope the layer to /mcp, or correct the comment to say it is router-wide. Which?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Correct the comment. It is the smaller behavioural change, and an unauthenticated health endpoint carrying an accurate protocol-version header is harmless.
